dataset.name: Community Based Data of Uranium Adsorption onto Quartz
description: This data upload includes a compilation of experiments for quantifying uranium adsorption onto quartz. The provided .csv file has been compiled from the literature in a findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable (FAIR) data format. This was accomplished using the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory Surface Complexation Database Converter (SCDC) code written in the R programming language (free licensing available at https://ipo.llnl.gov/technologies/software/llnl-surface-complexation-database-converter-scdc). This constitutes all current data compiled on uranium-quartz interactions in the L-SCIE (LLNL Surface Complexation/Ion Exchange) database (as of 02/28/2022). This data was used to develop surface complexation models that fit the global community dataset (https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.1c07109). The FAIR-formatted dataset also enables the implementation of alternative machine-learning approaches that can be explored in the future.

measurementTechnique:
The LLNL Surface Complexation Database Converter (SCDC) was used to compile community data metal-mineral adsorption experiments. The LLNL SCDC code written in R is available at the following link: https://ipo.llnl.gov/technologies/software/llnl-surface-complexation-database-converter-scdc.
Step 1 includes the digitization of journal manuscripts, including metadata information such as the DOI and original image files. Additionally, data values were also extracted using the DataThief software. Data included values of Kd, logKd, % sorbed, and mol/g surface excess values.

CSV files of compiled data and CSV files of metadata were unified into a single database. This combined file is stored in a Microsoft ACCESS database format. The master database is known as the LLNL Surface Complexation/Ion Exchange (L-SCIE) database.
Data has been filtered using the LLNL SCDC to extract available uranium-quartz adsorption experimental data. This filtered CSV file is available in this current data release.

A deeper description of the methodology can be found via Zavarin, Chang et al. 2022.
